name: SEPA Direct Debit return codes with collect-again defaults
licenseScope: CC BY 4.0 covers Waverunner's own defaults and text, not the codes, names and types from the EPC guidance and the ISO 20022 code set.
note: Codes, names, types and possible causes follow the European Payments Council (EPC) reason-code guidance v8.1 (30 September 2026). Whether to collect a returned debit again, and how long to wait first, are Waverunner defaults, not EPC rules.

sources.title: EPC173-14 Guidance on Reason Codes for SDD R-transactions, version 8.1
SEPA Direct Debit Core Scheme Rulebook 2025, version 1.1

codes.name: Incorrect Account Number

collectAgain.decision: Not until the IBAN is corrected

codes.description: AC01 means the account number (IBAN) on the debit is incorrect. Get the right IBAN from the customer before you collect again.
codes.whoCaused: The customer or you. The customer may have given wrong details, or your customer database may hold a wrong IBAN. A technical problem when you issued the collection can also cause it, and the code alone does not say which.
codes.collectAgainDetail: Not until the IBAN is corrected. Ask the customer for the right account number before the next debit. On Mollie, an AC01 may cancel the subscription at once.
codes.customerMessage: Your payment of [amount] on [date] did not go through because the bank did not accept the account number. Update your bank details here: [link].

codes.name: Closed Account Number

collectAgain.decision: Not from the closed account

codes.description: The customer closed the bank account behind an AC04 return. Ask them for a new account before collecting again; Mollie may cancel the subscription at once.
codes.whoCaused: The customer. They closed the account after your previous collection from it, so this debit went to details that no longer work.
codes.collectAgainDetail: Waverunner's default is no collection from the closed account. Mollie may cancel the subscription at once after an AC04.
codes.customerMessage: We could not collect [amount] on [date] because the bank account is closed. Add a different account here: [link].

codes.name: Blocked Account

collectAgain.decision: Not from the blocked account

codes.description: AC06 tells you the customer's bank blocked the account. Ask the customer for another account or way to pay; Mollie may cancel the subscription at once.
codes.whoCaused: The customer's bank. It blocked the account or this collection under a court order, or blocked the account over suspected misuse or at the customer's request.
codes.collectAgainDetail: Not from the blocked account. Ask the customer for another account or another way to pay. If you collect through Mollie, AC06 may cancel the subscription straight away.
codes.customerMessage: The [amount] payment due on [date] could not be taken from this account. Choose another way to pay here: [link].

codes.name: Invalid Debtor Account Type
codes.possibleCause: The customer or the account type

collectAgain.decision: Not as a B2B debit

codes.description: AC13 comes back when a B2B direct debit reaches a consumer account. Agree another way to pay, or a Core mandate, with the customer before collecting again.
codes.whoCaused: Two of the three causes sit with the customer. A consumer may have signed a B2B mandate without knowing it is only for non-consumers, or given details of the wrong account. The third, an account type that cannot take B2B debits, names no party.
codes.collectAgainDetail: Not as a B2B debit. Agree another way to pay, or a Core mandate, with the customer first.
codes.customerMessage: We could not collect [amount] on [date] because your account does not accept the business direct debit we set up. Choose another way to pay here: [link].

codes.name: Transaction Forbidden

collectAgain.decision: Not from that account

codes.description: With AG01, the account cannot take direct debits for regulatory reasons, a savings account for example. Agree another account or way to pay first.
codes.whoCaused: The customer, who gave you an account that direct debits cannot be taken from. The limit is the account type, for example a savings account.
codes.collectAgainDetail: Not from that account. We suggest agreeing another account or another payment method with the customer before the next debit.
codes.customerMessage: Your account type does not allow direct debits, so we could not collect [amount] on [date]. Choose another account or way to pay here: [link].

codes.name: Invalid Bank Operation Code

collectAgain.decision: Not until the operation code, sequence or file information is fixed

codes.description: AG02 flags a wrong operation code, sequence type or file format in your collection. Correct the collection data before you submit it again.
codes.whoCaused: You, as the creditor: a technical error, or a mistake in the collection or its file sequence. It covers a recurring debit sent after a one-off, a one-off sent after a recurring one, and a wrong scheme identification code.
codes.collectAgainDetail: Not until the operation code, sequence or file information is fixed. Your provider can help you find the wrong field.

codes.name: Insufficient Funds

collectAgain.decision: Yes, at most 2 times, when your notice period and our 5-day wait have both run

codes.description: AM04 means insufficient funds. Our default: tell the customer the new date, then collect again when your notice period ends, at most twice.
codes.whoCaused: The customer or you. The customer's account can be short of funds, or you may have sent the pre-notification late or not at all.
codes.collectAgainDetail: Waverunner's default is at most two new attempts, each at least 5 days after you send the pre-notification with the new date. Core, the scheme open to consumers and businesses, needs that pre-notification at least 14 calendar days before collection unless you agreed a different period. Stripe can retry at most twice within 30 days of the original attempt if Direct Debit retries are enabled. Mollie may retry subscriptions up to 5 times, once daily, depending on the failure reason; check your provider's schedule before adding your own attempt.
codes.customerMessage: Your payment of [amount] on [date] did not go through. Tell us here when your account will have funds: [link]. We will confirm the new collection date with you before we collect again.

codes.name: Duplication

collectAgain.decision: No, not this attempt

codes.description: AM05 flags a debit as a duplicate of one sent very recently. Stop this attempt and check whether the original debit already covers the payment.
codes.whoCaused: Possibly you or your bank: a technical or human error on your side can send the same collection twice.
codes.collectAgainDetail: No, not this attempt. Check whether the original payment already arrived, then decide whether anything is still due.

codes.name: Unrecognised Initiating Party

collectAgain.decision: Only once the creditor identifier is corrected

codes.description: BE05 points to your creditor identifier: it is wrong, or it changed without an amendment being reported. Correct it before collecting again.
codes.whoCaused: You: either a technical error, or a change to your creditor identifier that was never reported as an amendment.
codes.collectAgainDetail: Only once the creditor identifier is corrected. If the identifier changed, ask your provider how to report the amendment.

codes.name: Creditor Bank Is Not Registered

collectAgain.decision: Not until your bank's registration is fixed

codes.description: CNOR means your bank is not registered in the clearing system under the BIC it used. Ask your provider to fix the registration before resubmitting.
codes.whoCaused: Your bank, which is not, or no longer, declared as an indirect participant in the clearing system.
codes.collectAgainDetail: Not until your bank's registration is fixed. Once your provider confirms it, submit the collection again.

codes.name: Debtor Bank Is Not Registered

collectAgain.decision: Not by the same route until reachability is fixed

codes.description: DNOR means the customer's bank is not registered in the clearing system under its BIC. Ask your provider to check that the bank can be reached.
codes.whoCaused: You or your bank. The customer's bank is the one not registered, but the cause is on your side: you or your bank did not check beforehand that it could be reached.
codes.collectAgainDetail: Not by the same route until reachability is fixed. Ask your provider to check the customer's bank; if it cannot be reached, agree another way to pay with the customer.
codes.customerMessage: We could not collect [amount] on [date] through your bank. Choose another way to pay here: [link].

codes.name: Settlement Failed

collectAgain.decision: Yes, once, after your provider confirms settlement can go ahead, when your notice period and our 2-day wait have both run

codes.description: ED05 means settlement between the banks failed. Our default is one retry, once your provider confirms the debit can settle and your notice period has run.
codes.whoCaused: The customer's bank. Its funding for settling direct debits with other banks was not enough for this transaction.
codes.collectAgainDetail: Yes, once, after your provider confirms that settlement can go ahead. Then pre-notify the customer of the new date: a Core debit needs that notice at least 14 calendar days ahead unless you agreed a different period. Our 2-day wait runs from the same day, so the notice sets the date unless it is shorter than 2 days.

codes.name: Invalid File Format

collectAgain.decision: After the XML file is repaired

codes.description: FF01 rejects a collection file whose XML is invalid. Repair the file, or the validation check that missed it, with your provider before resending.
codes.whoCaused: You, your bank or the clearing system. The XML may be filled in wrongly or contain a syntax error. Or your bank, an intermediary bank or the clearing system skipped the validation check before submitting the file.
codes.collectAgainDetail: After the XML file is repaired. Work through the file error with your provider; the customer has nothing to correct for FF01.

codes.name: No Mandate

collectAgain.decision: No, not until you have a valid mandate

codes.description: MD01 means no valid mandate covers the debit. Stop collecting until you have one; as a refund, MD01 applies to Core collections only.
codes.whoCaused: Check the bank's mandate status, the customer's cancellation or B2B confirmation, and the mandate reference you sent. MD01 alone does not identify which party needs to act.
codes.collectAgainDetail: No, not until you have a valid mandate. Stop collecting meanwhile, including while a B2B confirmation or a reference fix is pending. Mollie may cancel the subscription after the third MD01.
codes.customerMessage: Your bank reported a problem with the direct debit authorisation for the [amount] debit dated [date]. Review or renew your authorisation here: [link].

codes.name: Missing Mandatory Mandate Information in Mandate

collectAgain.decision: Not until the mandate amendment or its data is repaired

codes.description: MD02 means mandate data is missing or incorrect. Repair the amendment details, or the way they were submitted, before sending another collection.
codes.whoCaused: No party is named. The amendment either did not follow the scheme rules, or the amended information is wrong.
codes.collectAgainDetail: Not until the mandate amendment or its data is repaired. Your provider can help you check what you submitted against the mandate you hold.

codes.name: Refund Request By End Customer

collectAgain.decision: Not automatically

codes.description: With MD06, the customer had a Core debit refunded. Talk to them before you collect again; Waverunner recommends no automatic retry of that debit.
codes.whoCaused: The cause is either a debit that did not match the amount in your pre-notification, or the customer's unconditional right to a refund. A refund request alone does not mean you made a mistake.
codes.collectAgainDetail: Waverunner recommends no automatic retry of the refunded debit. Contact the customer and agree how to continue. After a Stripe dispute, check whether Stripe deactivated a mandate covering repeat payments; if so, the customer must accept it again before you collect. Mollie may cancel the subscription after 3 MD06 failures.
codes.customerMessage: Your [amount] debit dated [date] was refunded. If you want to continue, tell us how you would like to pay here: [link].

codes.name: End Customer Deceased

collectAgain.decision: No

codes.description: MD07 reports that the customer has died. Stop collecting and close the agreement with the deceased customer instead of sending another payment request.
codes.whoCaused: No party is named.
codes.collectAgainDetail: No. Stop collecting and close the agreement. Mollie may cancel the subscription as soon as MD07 arrives.

codes.name: Not Specified Reason Customer Generated

collectAgain.decision: Not before you talk to the customer

codes.description: MS02 means the customer refused the debit after your pre-notification. Talk to them before another debit; Mollie may cancel after 3 such failures.
codes.whoCaused: The customer refused the collection.
codes.collectAgainDetail: For MS02, Waverunner's default is customer agreement before another debit. Mollie may cancel the subscription after 3 MS02 failures.
codes.customerMessage: Your [amount] debit dated [date] was not completed. Tell us here how you would like to handle this payment: [link].

codes.name: Not Specified Reason Agent Generated

collectAgain.decision: After asking, then once, when your notice period and our 7-day wait have both run

codes.description: MS03 comes with no specific reason from the bank. Ask the customer or your provider which reason applies before the one retry our default allows.
codes.whoCaused: Who is at fault depends on the hidden reason. Where national law bars the specific code, MS03 can stand in for AC04, AM04, MD07, RR01, RR02, RR03 or RR04: a closed account, insufficient funds, a deceased account holder, missing details or another regulatory reason. In Germany, for example, a bank returning a debit for insufficient funds (AM04) sends MS03 instead, though AM04 can still arrive from outside Germany. Sparkasse KölnBonn also reports a deceased account holder (MD07) and another regulatory reason (RR04) as MS03, for data-protection reasons.
codes.collectAgainDetail: Not before you ask the customer or your provider which reason applies: a closed account needs new details, and a death means closing the agreement. If neither applies and you still want to collect, our default is one retry. Send your pre-notification and collect when its notice period ends: at least 14 calendar days for a Core debit unless you agreed a different one, and never sooner than 7 days. Mollie may cancel a subscription after 3 failures with MS03.
codes.customerMessage: Your bank returned the [amount] payment from [date] without giving a reason. If your payment details have changed or you want to talk about this payment, reach us here: [link].

codes.name: Bank Identifier Incorrect

collectAgain.decision: After the BIC is corrected

codes.description: RC01 points to a wrong BIC (bank identifier code), including an incomplete one on a non-EEA collection. Ask your provider to correct it.
codes.whoCaused: It depends where the BIC went wrong. You caused it if you gave an incomplete BIC, 8 characters instead of 11, for a non-EEA collection. Your bank, the clearing system or the customer's bank caused it if the BIC in the interbank message does not exist.
codes.collectAgainDetail: After the BIC is corrected. Ask your provider to put the complete, correct BIC in the message, and ask the customer for theirs on a non-EEA collection.
codes.customerMessage: We need to check your bank details before we can collect [amount], due on [date]. Confirm them here: [link].

codes.name: Missing Debtor Account Or Identification

collectAgain.decision: Not until the account or identification data is complete

codes.description: RR01 comes back when customer account or identification details that regulation requires are missing. Complete the data with your provider first.
codes.whoCaused: No party is named. The customer's IBAN or unique identification, needed for regulatory requirements, is missing or insufficient.
codes.collectAgainDetail: Not until the account or identification data is complete. Your provider can tell you what is missing so you can complete the collection record.
codes.customerMessage: Some payment details are missing, so we could not collect [amount] on [date]. Complete them here: [link].

codes.name: Missing Debtor Name Or Address

collectAgain.decision: Only after the name or address information is corrected

codes.description: RR02 flags customer name or address details that are missing, insufficient or invalid. Correct the collection details with your provider first.
codes.whoCaused: Nobody is named. The customer's name or address, needed for regulatory requirements, is missing or insufficient. The code does not say whether you or the customer left it out.
codes.collectAgainDetail: Only after the name or address information is corrected. Ask your provider which information or address format it needs, then update the collection record.
codes.customerMessage: Before we can collect [amount], due on [date], we need to check your name and address. Review them here: [link].

codes.name: Missing Creditor Name Or Address

collectAgain.decision: Not until your creditor information is corrected

codes.description: RR03 points to your own creditor name or address details, which need correcting. Fix your business information with your payment provider first.
codes.whoCaused: No party is named, but the data at fault is your own: your creditor name or address.
codes.collectAgainDetail: Not until your creditor information is corrected. Fix the business name or address format with your provider; the customer has no bank details to change.

codes.name: Regulatory Reason

collectAgain.decision: Not for now

codes.description: RR04 stops a debit for a regulatory reason other than missing account, name or address details. Stop collecting and ask your provider why.
codes.whoCaused: No party, and no cause is given: RR04 covers regulatory reasons other than those RR01, RR02 and RR03 cover.
codes.collectAgainDetail: Not for now. Stop collecting until your provider explains which restriction applies and what, if anything, would resolve it.

codes.name: Specific Service Offered By Debtor Agent

collectAgain.decision: Not before you talk to the customer

codes.description: SL01 means a service at the customer's bank, such as a creditor block or an amount limit, stopped the debit. Ask the customer before another debit.
codes.whoCaused: SL01 names no party. The cause is a service on the customer's bank account, such as a block they set against you or a limit on amount or frequency.
codes.collectAgainDetail: Not before you talk to the customer. We recommend agreeing with them how to pay, because the bank's block or limit may still apply. Three SL01 failures may end a Mollie subscription.
codes.customerMessage: A block or limit on your bank account stopped the [amount] debit on [date]. Tell us how you would like to pay here: [link].
